44f34c709156.text: Welcome, everyone! Today I want to walk you through a paper Amrit Tiwana and I wrote: Dynamics of Mirroring.

af185ad248fe.text: It's about how open-source teams and their code grow up together.

8d9e3ca29a42.text: And it ends with a surprising idea: a little misalignment can be good for a project.

bb60c6395d6c.text: Let's start with the mirroring hypothesis.

1af2839a0dd2.text: It says the structure of a team should mirror the structure of the product it builds.

4d523fd01b6f.text: If Alice builds the user interface and Bob builds the data layer, they barely need to talk...

7d41f11145c2.text: ...because the interface between their modules does the coordinating for them.

8587542fb5ad.text: Ties between people line up with dependencies between modules. That's mirroring.

9e4b47c8ccd5.text: It saves scarce attention, and mirrored systems tend to be more successful.

8b32099c1cac.text: But here's the puzzle. Open-source software is famously modular...

6e3475750b4e.text: ...and its developers specialize. So we'd expect strong mirroring.

694813929ca0.text: Yet in a major review, 56% of studies of open collaboration found no support for it.

e4b30c3e989c.text: So why does mirroring seem to vanish in open source?

903bfa1fa53a.text: One answer: the code itself coordinates people, so they don't need to talk.

e054d1e93549.text: Another: digital tools stand in for sitting in the same building.

cc5d177089fb.text: We asked a different question. What if we've been looking at a snapshot...

224b8bd97047.text: ...when we should be watching the movie?

f575d6f2c6df.text: So we separate two things. The state of mirroring is how well team and code match right now.

d70747d1d328.text: We measure each structure's modularity, Q: zero for monolithic, one for fully modular.

fb445198bb81.text: Mirroring is high when the two Qs are close to each other.

7a2dfead8062.text: The dynamics are how that match changes from one quarter to the next.

c6bdd8652940.text: When the match improves, we call it mirror focusing.

62cd4c0d5db2.text: When it slips, we call it mirror misting, like breath fogging up a mirror.

c6ab2d1c0875.text: Picture a two-by-two: team structure across the top, project architecture down the side.

aa777bfa0902.text: In A, a monolithic team builds monolithic code. In D, a modular team builds modular code.

ac17a5ceaa7d.text: Both are mirrored. B and C are the mismatches.

bfdd3af808bd.text: Stepping out of A or D mists the mirror. Stepping back in focuses it.

0a923c89b071.text: That's eight possible moves: four mistings and four focusings.

d6ddbe47eba4.text: To watch this happen, we went straight to the source code.

e53b5d55e7aa.text: We studied 1,279 Java projects on GitHub...

e760b2ed7bb7.text: ...rebuilding every codebase quarter by quarter: 25,947 project-quarters in all.

a043c0a4bc78.text: No surveys. Every measure comes from the code and the commit logs themselves.

430d5c8337ed.text: Each quarter, we build three networks.

a7a240806729.text: First, the architecture: classes, linked when one uses or inherits from another.

a8d9ef48d13f.text: Second, the activity: which developers committed to which files.

93a742e5221b.text: Third, the team: two developers are linked when they change the same file.

ab538b903db5.text: The modularity of the first gives us the project architecture. The third gives us the team structure.

3f98e65c49af.text: As a state, mirroring is a little sticky from one quarter to the next...

95b24b96e2a6.text: ...but focusing is followed by misting, and misting by focusing. The coefficient is minus 0.41.

2698144b76b0.text: So weak mirroring in a snapshot may really be strong dynamics in motion.

8fcb89e91ea6.text: We measured two kinds of change. System-wide: files added or removed...

a96a57afc682.text: ...and module-level: code rewritten inside the files that stay.

d82662447b1c.text: Mirror focusing pushes both of them up, especially change inside modules.

69342bf87750.text: But a high, static mirroring state pushes evolution down. That's the mirroring trap.

85d99d1c8965.text: A perfectly matched project can freeze in place.

156b49637f65.text: Focusing pays off when it lands in D: a modular team on modular code.

c5efa879e821.text: B to D and C to D boost both kinds of evolution.

af5700cf7c2c.text: One exception: B to A helps change inside modules, but not across the whole system.

a874122a1481.text: So what does it all mean?

c07a6e88dc54.text: Misting isn't a failure. It's how developers explore, tinker, and learn other parts of the system.

cb5e312c993f.text: Focusing is where that learning gets put to work.

c0c0bc1a1040.text: Misting is a stressor that makes the project stronger. Taleb would call that antifragile.

75abf865de3a.text: For managers: don't lock the mirror in place. Leave room for bottom-up tinkering.

751c6b84dbb2.text: The future of mirroring research lies not in optimizing configurations...
